BUILD PART 1 OF 3 OF F2D PR1: rewrite migration 011 to one wide row per system, move the canonical archetype model into shared_contracts with the model digest, update the builder/validator/registration, and recut the manifest and authority. Base on current origin/main (record the SHA; it must include #806 at 95f532a and #808 at cd6ba81). New branch, no target_branch. Parts 2 and 3 will update this same branch later, so leave it in a state a follow-up can continue from.

AUTHORITY: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-v3-finder-f2d-wide-archetype-and-product-attachment-design.md is the specification. Read CLAUDE.md first, then design sections 1, 2, 3 (3.1-3.5), 4.3 (the model-digest rules only; the endpoint itself is PR3), 5 (5.1-5.3), 10 (the PR1 bullet list) and 12. Where this task and the design differ, the design wins. Where the design and the current code differ, follow the design and name the conflict in your summary. Do not reopen design decisions.

SCOPE OF THIS PART. Part 1 is the data layer only. Part 2 (a later task on this branch) does design section 6: apps/api/src/ranking/profile.py, ranking_sql.py, routers/archetypes.py, models.py, local_search.py and the regenerated clients. Part 3 does scripts/v3_archetype_calibration_probe.py, scripts/dev/measure_wide_archetype_footprint.py, scripts/dev/seed_v3_fixture_generation.py, scripts/dev/seed_cypress_v3_generation.py and their tests. DO NOT TOUCH any of those files in this part, and do not touch apps/web. Their tests (tests/test_ranking_*.py, tests/test_archetype_rankings_v3.py, tests/test_local_search_v3.py, tests/test_ranking_identity_and_no_legacy.py, tests/test_v3_archetype_calibration_probe*.py, tests/test_measure_wide_archetype_*.py, the seed test modules, Review Lab and Cypress) are EXPECTED to fail at this head because the schema changes under them. Do not edit, skip, xfail, mark or delete any of them; the follow-up parts fix them. No pull request will be opened until all three parts have landed.

ALLOWED FILES: sql/v3/migrations/011_v3_system_archetype.sql (rewritten in place); sql/v3/migration-manifest.txt; deploy/v3-production/target-authority.json; docs/operations/v3-production-application-release.md; shared_contracts/v3_system_archetype_model.py (new canonical model); scripts/v3_system_archetype_model.py (becomes a thin re-export of the canonical module); scripts/v3_system_archetype.py; scripts/operator/actions/v3-derived-lifecycle-status.sh (only if its pending-set contract pins migration hashes); tests/test_v3_system_archetype_migration.py, tests/test_v3_system_archetype_model.py, tests/test_v3_system_archetype_register.py, tests/test_v3_system_archetype_build.py, tests/test_v3_system_archetype_validate.py, tests/test_v3_system_archetype_cli.py; tests/test_v3_lineage_migrations.py, tests/test_v3_production_migration_operation.py, tests/test_v3_system_search_production_operator.py, tests/test_v3_watchlist_postgres.py, tests/test_v3_production_application_deployment.py (only where they pin the 011 hash or the migration-set/schema identities); tests/test_python314_execution_surfaces.py (only if the new module must be listed); CHANGES.md. Any other changed path must be justified in your summary as required by a specific failing contract test, otherwise it is a failure.

WHY 011 IS REWRITTEN IN PLACE: 011 is registered in the manifest but has never been applied to production (docs/ROADMAP.md, "Registration is not application"), so the design rewrites it rather than adding a corrective migration. Do not add a new migration number.

MIGRATION 011 (design section 3). (a) Replace the keyed v3_derived.system_archetype table and the v3_derived.system_archetype_summary table with the single wide table of section 3.1, the eight <key>_score / <key>_tier / <key>_confidence_ppm / <key>_weighted_e4 groups written out in ARCHETYPE_KEYS order (paradise, mining_hub, manufacturing_hub, megacomplex, research_hub, stronghold, population_capital, flexible), plus primary_archetype, secondary_archetype, best_colony_potential, best_tier, archetype_confidence_ppm, weighted_potential (double precision, unrounded), completeness_ppm, computed_at, the primary key, the deferrable FK to system_rating_vector and every CHECK listed there. (b) The weighted-key expression in SQL is exactly ((<key>_score::bigint * <key>_confidence_ppm * completeness_ppm) + 50000000) / 100000000 (bigint cast first; never round()). (c) No physical summary table: v3_app.system_archetype_summary becomes the view of section 3.2 and v3_app.system_archetype exposes every stored column plus the derived <key>_confidence doubles (ppm / 1000000.0). (d) Indexes per section 3.3: the primary key; (derived_generation_id, weighted_potential DESC NULLS LAST, system_id64); and for each of the eight keys three partial indexes (derived_generation_id, <key>_weighted_e4 DESC, system_id64) WHERE <key>_score >= 60 / >= 76 / >= 88 with the floor as a literal -- 26 physical indexes in all. (e) Keep v3_derived.archetype_build_chunk and all three mutation properties of section 3.5 (insert only while the product is BUILDING; UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE rejected; allowed attachment states BUILDING/VALIDATING/READY -- PUBLISHED is added by migration 015 in PR2, not here). Drop only the summary-table trigger target; rename no externally used guard.

CANONICAL MODEL (design sections 5.1 and 4.3). (a) Create shared_contracts/v3_system_archetype_model.py as the canonical model and make scripts/v3_system_archetype_model.py a thin re-export of it, so the API image (apps/api/Dockerfile copies shared_contracts) can import the model later. (b) ARCHETYPE_VERSION = 'v3-archetype-4'; coefficients and anchors unchanged. (c) One scoring entry point score_raw_system(vector_row, opportunity_groups) that takes the rating-vector row exactly as selected (all six arrays unscaled, as a named row) and the system's opportunity groups as integer triples (economy_ordinal, row_count, local_score_sum), and returns every value the wide row persists: all eight scores, tiers, confidence ppm and weighted keys, primary/secondary, best potential, best tier, archetype confidence ppm, weighted_potential and completeness_ppm. The scaling, the opportunity mean (local_score_sum / row_count, divided once), completeness_ppm = min(completeness array) * 100, the shared half-up ppm helper, fit_all, _fit_anchored, _fit_flexible, _quality, _clamp, tier_of, summarise, weighted_potential and the weighted-key integer expression (numerator + 50_000_000) // 100_000_000 are all reachable from it. (d) Move explanation construction out of the _fit_* functions into separate _explain_* functions. (e) Two module-level SQL constants are the complete query contracts: the vector read returning the six arrays unscaled in the order score_raw_system unpacks them, and the opportunity read returning count(*)::int and sum(local_score)::bigint per (system_id64, economy_ordinal) -- no avg, no float cast -- each with only the generation and the chunk or system as parameters. (f) archetype_model_sha256(): hash score_raw_system and every function reachable from it by walking the call graph (not a hand-maintained list), excluding the _explain_* functions; every module-level assignment a covered function reads (recursively) and every class the graph references; and the two SQL constants whitespace-collapsed. Each function is hashed as ast.dump(tree, include_attributes=False) with its docstring removed. The walk FAILS CLOSED: a reference to any name that is not a definition in the model module, a builtin, a member of math, or dataclasses.dataclass / dataclasses.field (resolved through the module's own import statement) makes the digest uncomputable and registration impossible. The digest excludes ARCHETYPE_VERSION, explanation construction, storage-shape constants and whole-file hashes.

BUILDER, MANIFEST, VALIDATOR in scripts/v3_system_archetype.py (design sections 5.1-5.3). (a) product_manifest() keeps what it hashes today and adds: a canonical ordered wide_columns list carrying the weighted-key integer expression verbatim, storage_layout 'one-row-per-system-v1', explanation_delivery 'on-demand', the confidence storage/rounding policy, model_file_sha256 (SHA-256 of the canonical module file), archetype_model_sha256, and the CPython version. (b) code_identity() hashes the canonical model file AND the re-export, alongside the builder and 011. (c) Build: per Ratings chunk, read raw vectors and integer groups through the two shared constants (pure fetch, no computation in SQL), call score_raw_system once per system, pivot into one wide tuple, insert one wide row per system and one archetype_build_chunk receipt in the same transaction; the chunk content_sha256 covers every persisted column in system_id64 order including archetype_version and one explicitly assigned computed_at per chunk. Keep the CLI flags and exit codes. (d) register_product and validate_product both require the same generation's system_search product READY with a VERIFIED receipt. (e) validate_product gates BUILDING -> READY on every item of section 5.3, calling the shared half-up helper rather than reimplementing rounding, re-deriving completeness_ppm from min(system_rating_vector.completeness) * 100 on the same generation, and checking every <key>_weighted_e4 against the integer expression on the STORED completeness_ppm. Both digests are persisted on the product row.

REGISTRATION RECUT. The rewritten 011 has a new SHA-256, so the registered lineage identity changes. Update sql/v3/migration-manifest.txt, deploy/v3-production/target-authority.json (compatible_migration_sets, schema_transition and every recomputed identity) and docs/operations/v3-production-application-release.md for the pending set [014, 010, 011-rewritten, 013], exactly the way PR #792 (commit c3da606) did it after rewriting 010 -- read that commit's diff first and mirror it. Update the hash/identity assertions in the listed tests. Do not change any other migration file.

TESTS TO WRITE OR UPDATE (runners have no PostgreSQL: write the database-backed tests against the existing disposable-PG18 fixtures used by the current archetype tests, run everything that runs without a database, and list the database tests you wrote but could not run). Required: (1) model: half-boundary vectors (a numerator landing exactly on 50_000_000, two keys with equal _weighted_e4 so system_id64 breaks the tie, the 0 and maximum ends) assert the same integer from the model, the SQL expression text and the validator rule; a 500,000-random-triple comparison of the integer rule against score * confidence * completeness in floating point with zero disagreements at non-tie inputs; (2) digest: unchanged by an edit confined to an _explain_* function and by a comment/docstring/formatting-only edit to a covered function; changed by an edit to each covered member and to each clause of each SQL constant; changed by a referenced global's value or a referenced class; the unchanged canonical model produces a digest; a scoring function that calls an imported repository helper, or a dataclass imported from anywhere but dataclasses, makes the computation fail; (3) code_identity changes when only the canonical file is edited; (4) migration: both views exist and every projected column selects; exactly 26 indexes with the stated definitions and literal floors; the three mutation guards hold; the summary table is gone; (5) validator: the existing eight-rows-plus-summary coverage tests become per-column wide-row tests; a half-boundary row is accepted; a wrong stored completeness_ppm, a wrong weighted key, a missing chunk receipt, a count mismatch and an unverified Search each fail; (6) the committed database-shaped frozen fixture of section 5.3: raw system_rating_vector and economy_opportunity rows, including an opportunity group whose mean is not exactly representable (local scores 1, 1, 2), read through the builder's real chunk read, scored by score_raw_system, compared on every persisted column; a unit test drives score_raw_system from the same rows' integer groups and must agree.

VALIDATION TO RUN AND REPORT WITH EXACT COUNTS: ruff check scripts shared_contracts tests apps/api/src; python -m pytest tests/test_v3_system_archetype_model.py tests/test_python314_execution_surfaces.py -q; every other test module you touched that runs without a database; sha256sum of the rewritten 011 against the manifest line; the recomputed migration-set identity against the authority file. Do not deploy, contact production, or use production credentials. Preserve fail-closed validation and bounded inputs; parameterized SQL only.

IF YOU CANNOT FINISH EVERYTHING IN THIS SESSION, complete in this order and stop cleanly: migration 011, canonical model + digest, builder/validator, recut, tests. State precisely what remains so the follow-up task can complete it. End with: files changed; tests run with counts; database tests written but not run; what is deferred to parts 2 and 3; and any design-versus-code conflict you found.
